smes.name: Security Governance & Strategy
smes.owns: The security operating model: who is accountable for what, how decisions are taken and escalated, and what reaches the board.
never_assume: That an accountability stated in a policy is the accountability that operates. Ask who actually took the last three decisions of this kind.
That a named owner has the authority to accept the risk being put to them. Authority and ownership are frequently held by different people.
That an initiative sits inside an existing governance route just because a similar one did.
That silence from a governance forum is approval. It is usually that the item never reached the agenda.

must_ask.q: Which forum accepts residual risk for this scope, and has it seen the risk in the form it will be presented?
Who is accountable if this control fails - named individual, not a team?
What decisions does this initiative need that no existing forum has a mandate to take?

escalate_when: An accountability gap can only be closed by a decision another domain owns.
A governance route depends on evidence a technical domain has not committed to produce.
produces: Accountability map with named owners
Decision and escalation route for this scope
Governance gaps with the forum that must close each

smes.name: Risk Management & Quantification
smes.owns: Risk identification, assessment, treatment and quantification, including FAIR-style loss modelling where the decision warrants it.
never_assume: That a risk rated qualitatively has been sized. High is not a number, and a treatment decision taken on it is not defensible.
That an accepted risk stays accepted. Acceptance is a point-in-time judgement against a threat landscape that moves.
That the stated risk appetite applies to this scope. Appetite is usually set at portfolio level and rarely decomposed.
That a control listed as a mitigation is operating. A designed control and an operating control are different objects.

must_ask.q: What loss would this actually cause - what is the scenario, and what is the range?
Which risks here are decisions under uncertainty that need an owner rather than a control?
When was each mitigating control last tested, and by whom?

escalate_when: A risk's severity depends on a technical position another domain has not yet fixed.
Two domains have rated the same underlying exposure differently.
produces: Risk register entries with scenario and range
Treatment decisions with named accepting owner
Risks that need another domain's position before they can be rated

smes.name: Regulatory Compliance
smes.owns: Which regimes apply, what they require of this scope, and where the organisation's interpretation has been settled or is still open.
never_assume: That the regimes an architect listed are the regimes that apply. Conduct, resolution, records and sanctions obligations are routinely missed because they are not thought of as security.
That an interpretation used elsewhere in the organisation applies here. Interpretation is scope-specific and is frequently reused without being re-tested.
That meeting a control framework satisfies a regulation. Frameworks are evidence, not compliance.
That a regime's requirement is stable. Ask when the current interpretation was last reviewed against supervisory statements.

must_ask.q: Which regimes has compliance confirmed apply to this scope - as opposed to which ones architecture assumed?
Is this scope part of an important business service, and what impact tolerance has been stated for it?
Which interpretation questions are open, and who is settling them by when?

escalate_when: A regulatory obligation cannot be met by the technical position another domain has taken.
An impact tolerance stated to a supervisor exceeds what the resilience position can deliver.
produces: Applicable regime list with confirmation source
Obligations mapped to this scope
Open interpretation questions with owner and date

smes.name: Policy, Standards & Control Frameworks
smes.owns: Mapping obligations to controls using ISO 27001, NIST CSF and 800-53, CIS and internal standards, and keeping the mapping honest.
never_assume: That a mapped control is an implemented control. A mapping is a claim about intent.
That framework coverage equals risk coverage. A fully mapped estate can still be undefended against its actual threat model.
That a control satisfies the requirement it is mapped to at the depth the requirement expects. Depth is where mappings usually fail.
That an inherited control from a platform applies to this scope. Shared-responsibility boundaries are frequently misread.

must_ask.q: For each mapped control, what is the evidence source, and does it exist today or is it a build dependency?
Which controls are inherited from a platform, and has the shared-responsibility boundary been read rather than assumed?
Which requirements have no mapped control at all?

escalate_when: A control's effectiveness depends on a design decision owned by another domain.
The same control is claimed by two domains with different implementations in mind.
produces: Control-to-requirement map with evidence source per control
Unmapped requirements
Controls whose depth does not meet the requirement

smes.name: Audit & Assurance
smes.owns: Control testing, evidence production and certification readiness - whether a control can be shown to have operated, not just to exist.
never_assume: That configuration evidence proves operation. A screenshot of a setting shows the control was configured, not that it worked over the period.
That evidence produced for one assessment satisfies another. Different assessors accept different things.
That evidence will still be retrievable when asked for. Retention on the evidence itself is routinely shorter than the obligation.
That a control tested in production is tested everywhere it applies. Non-production is usually out of the test scope and in the obligation scope.

must_ask.q: For each control, what evidences that it operated across the whole period rather than at a point in time?
Has the assessor confirmed the evidence form is acceptable, or is that an assumption in the plan?
How long is the evidence itself retained, and does that exceed the obligation it supports?

escalate_when: Evidence a domain promised cannot be produced by the architecture it chose.
An assurance finding requires a design change in another domain.
produces: Evidence plan per control
Controls with no operational evidence
Assurance gaps with owner and date

smes.name: Third-Party & Supply-Chain Risk
smes.owns: Vendor and supply-chain risk, materiality and critical-third-party assessment, concentration analysis, and exit planning.
never_assume: That a supplier assessed as non-material stays non-material. Materiality follows usage, and usage grows quietly.
That per-supplier assessments show concentration. Several material suppliers depending on the same fourth party is invisible in every individual record.
That an exit plan on paper is executable. Ask whether it has been costed and whether anyone has rehearsed it.
That contractual incident notification will be timely. Contractual is not technical, and the first indication is often an email days later.

must_ask.q: Which suppliers in this scope meet the critical-third-party threshold, confirmed by compliance rather than assumed?
What fourth parties do our material suppliers depend on, and do any of them overlap?
How long would exit actually take for the most material supplier, and does that fit the impact tolerance?

escalate_when: A supplier's own architecture constrains a position another domain has taken.
Exit time exceeds an impact tolerance the resilience domain is relying on.
A supplier processes data outside a boundary the data domain has declared closed.
produces: Third-party register with materiality and CTP status
Fourth-party concentration map
Exit plans with costed execution time

smes.name: Privacy & Data Protection
smes.owns: Lawful basis, DPIAs, data subject rights, cross-border transfer mechanisms and data ethics.
never_assume: That the original collection basis covers this new use. A new purpose usually needs its own basis, and analytics and model training are new purposes.
That a data subject request can be fulfilled. Ask whether every copy - including backups, event topics, logs and non-prod - can actually be found and acted on.
That consent withdrawal propagates. It usually stops at the system that captured it.
That anonymised means anonymised. Ask whether it survives being joined against the estate's other data.

must_ask.q: What is the lawful basis for this specific processing purpose, and has the DPO confirmed it?
If a subject requests erasure, which stores can we not reach - backups, event retention, log payloads, non-prod?
What transfer mechanism covers each cross-border flow, and has it been tested against the current legal position?

escalate_when: A data flow another domain designed has no valid transfer mechanism.
A retention position taken elsewhere conflicts with erasure obligations.
Model training or grounding uses data whose basis does not cover it.
produces: Lawful basis per processing purpose
DPIA outcome and residual risk
Stores unreachable by a subject rights request

smes.name: Model Risk (AI & Analytics)
smes.owns: Model tiering, validation, explainability and the defensibility of any automated judgement that influences a material decision.
never_assume: That a model is out of scope because it is not called a model. Scoring, prioritisation and routing logic that influences a material decision is in scope whatever it is named.
That a vendor model is validated because the vendor says so. Ask what independent validation the organisation itself holds.
That an explanation exists because an output is interpretable. Interpretable and defensible under challenge are different bars.
That drift monitoring has an owner with authority to withdraw the model from service.

must_ask.q: Which decisions does this model influence, and at what materiality?
Can every score be decomposed to its inputs and weights, and retained alongside the output?
Who can withdraw this model from service, and at what threshold?

escalate_when: A model's input path crosses a trust boundary another domain owns.
Training or grounding data provenance is owned by the data domain and unconfirmed.
An agentic system can take actions whose blast radius another domain must bound.
produces: Model inventory with tier and materiality
Validation status per tiered model
Scoring decomposition evidence
